summary: Asks that proposed protocols from now on be submitted as on-line documents, preferably NLS files at the Network Information Center, so they can be reviewed, edited, updated and distributed quickly. It also carries a note to Telnet protocol readers and implementers.

eli5.summary: The rule is to send your protocol ideas as files in the shared computer system, not on paper, so everyone can read and fix them fast.

subtitle: Jon Postel asks for protocol proposals as on-line documents and flags a Telnet subnegotiation change.

tldr.problem: Reviewing and updating proposed protocols on paper was slow.
tldr.mechanism: Proposed protocols are to be submitted as on-line documents, preferably NLS files at the Network Information Center. The note also says Telnet subnegotiation strings end with IAC SE.
tldr.outcome: On-line documents are easy to review, edit, update and distribute; RFC 582 later updated this note.

today: RFC 580 has no formal status recorded and was updated by RFC 582.

sections.title: On-Line Protocol Documents
sections.content:
Hereafter, proposed protocols shall be submitted as on-line documents, preferably as NLS files at the Network Information Center. The note says this greatly facilitates the review process and lets editorial and substantive changes proceed quickly. It also permits timely updating as future decisions require, and on-line documents are easily distributed to the network community.

Anyone with great difficulty in complying is asked to contact the author.
sections.eli5: Put your ideas in the shared computer instead of on paper, so changes are fast.

sections.title: Telnet Subnegotiation Change
sections.content:
All existing Telnet Options that involve subnegotiation are modified (see RFC 562) to terminate the subnegotiation strings with IAC SE. The value of SE is 240.

Within subnegotiations, a byte with the value 255 (IAC) must be doubled on transmission.
sections.eli5: Special messages now end with a clear stop sign, and if the message needs the stop sign's own symbol inside it, you write that symbol twice.

sections.title: Contact Details
sections.content: The note ends with a change of address for Jon Postel, now at The MITRE Corporation in McLean, Virginia. On-line messages reach him as POSTEL@ISI or as JBP in the NIC Journal.
sections.eli5: It also tells people the new address for reaching the author.

references.text: Modifications to the Telnet specification, RFC 562.
